concept: AI-native streaming and generative UI interaction deltas
summary: Source-anchored research for AI-native streaming and generative UI interaction deltas. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Generative UI changes the response from text in a predefined interface into an interface generated at the time of use, including interactive tools or simulations; Google Research describes this implementation, while Google Cloud distinguishes component selection, declarative descriptions, and open-ended generated code. (medium confidence)

Apple advises communicating that AI-generated content may contain errors. This is an uncertainty disclosure recommendation, not a claim that the interface can estimate factual accuracy. (low confidence)

Google Cloud recommends streaming UI updates to begin rendering while generation continues, because the additional reasoning step affects time to interaction. This is implementation guidance, not a measured guarantee that streaming improves task performance. (low confidence)

Streak separately reports an invalid generated citation URL that combined parts of two supplied keys and produced a missing-page error. A displayed citation is therefore insufficient evidence of a valid destination in that implementation; its reference-map approach addresses a different problem from visual streaming polish. (low confidence)

NN/G observed that forced autoscroll during streaming disrupted reading and could make participants wait for completion. It recommends preserving the beginning of a long new response instead of jumping to its end. (low confidence)

Redis’s engineering guidance warns that an interrupted or failed stream can appear to be a successful partial answer unless the frontend distinguishes connection loss from an explicit error in the stream. The interaction needs a visible incomplete/error state rather than treating received text as proof of completion. (low confidence)

NN/G’s 2024 generative-UI article anticipates a consistency tradeoff: repeatedly changing layouts can require users to relearn an interface. It presents this as a predicted design challenge, not an observed universal failure of generated interfaces. (low confidence)

For uncertainty and failure fallback at the response level, Babich’s practitioner guidance recommends clear expectations, an undo, and a manual fallback for AI features. This remains a design prescription rather than evidence that a specific fallback has been evaluated. (low confidence)

NN/G recommends clickable follow-up suggestions instead of text that users must retype, but also warns against repeating suggestions users have already declined to engage with. This supports progressive exploration without repeatedly prompting the same next step. (low confidence)
Apple recommends a non-AI fallback when possible; this is qualified guidance rather than a requirement that every generative feature have a substitute. (low confidence)

Nielsen Norman Group recommends expanding and collapsing additional product details in place. In its observed Rufus interaction, a More details link instead appended a new chat message, pushing the comparison list out of view; the in-place alternative is a recommendation, not a reported comparative trial result. (low confidence)

Streak’s engineering account reports that incomplete Markdown citation links briefly exposed long raw URLs before collapsing to link text. Its constrained-format solution buffered the URL until the link closed, then substituted an application-owned reference mapping and emitted the completed link. (low confidence)

Nick Babich’s November 2026 practitioner guidance recommends traceable inline citations that open the source and highlight the passage, and cautions against presenting a bare confidence percentage without explaining where data came from. These are attributed design recommendations, not validated effect sizes. (low confidence)

In assistant-ui issue 1718, a contributor attributed disappearing tool UI to a custom adapter recreating the content array on each chunk, losing previous tool calls. The contributor recommended accumulating tool calls outside the loop; this account does not establish installed release behavior. (low confidence)

Google Research’s reported preference evaluation favored generated interfaces over standard LLM formats but explicitly excluded generation speed; it therefore does not establish an end-to-end latency-inclusive advantage. The same report acknowledged occasional output inaccuracies. (low confidence)

Streaming needs rendering decisions as well as early output: Google Cloud recommends incremental UI updates for responsiveness, while Streak reports that incomplete streamed Markdown links briefly exposed raw URLs before collapsing into formatted citations. These sources support treating intermediate presentation as a design state. (medium confidence)

For source navigation, Streak reports replacing model-generated long citation URLs with short references mapped to original links. This is an implementation report about citation delivery, not evidence that a cited answer is factually correct. (low confidence)
Apple’s generative-AI design guidance says specific feedback during generation reduces uncertainty and makes waiting feel purposeful. (low confidence)
